#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PCP-003"
UO = "bioreactor"
UO_TITLE = "Production Bioreactor (Step 3)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ---
import itertools as _it

UOP = CFG.unit_op(UO)
params = UOP.parameters
n_par = len(params)
n_mv = sum(1 for p in params if p.study == "multivariate")
n_uv = n_par - n_mv

scr_f = D.screening_factors(UO)
rsm_f = D.rsm_factors(UO)
n_scr_f = len(scr_f)
n_rsm_f = len(rsm_f)
resps = D.responses(UO)
n_resp = len(resps)
n_cqa_set = len(cqas_for(UO))

_scr = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
_rsm = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
n_scr = doe_runs(UO, "screening")
n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
n_scr_cen = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening")
n_rsm_cen = doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
n_scr_fac = int((_scr.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_fac = int((_rsm.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_ax = int((_rsm.run_type == "axial").sum())

# Model size and the degrees of freedom each design leaves. These are properties of the
# DESIGN, so they are available before any run is executed and belong in a protocol.
n_scr_terms = 1 + n_scr_f + len(list(_it.combinations(scr_f, 2)))
n_rsm_terms = 1 + 2 * n_rsm_f + len(list(_it.combinations(rsm_f, 2)))
scr_res_df = n_scr - n_scr_terms
rsm_res_df = n_rsm - n_rsm_terms
scr_pe_df = n_scr_cen - 1
rsm_pe_df = n_rsm_cen - 1
scr_lof_df = scr_res_df - scr_pe_df
rsm_lof_df = rsm_res_df - rsm_pe_df

n_uv_cond = 2 * n_uv                       # low edge + high edge for each univariate parameter
n_runs_total = n_scr + n_rsm + n_uv_cond

dur_sp = UOP.param("duration").setpoint
scale_l = V["commercial_scale_l"]
n_mc = V["n_monte_carlo"]
n_ppq = V["n_ppq"]
par_grid = D.PAR_GRID
par_mc = D.PAR_MC_N

# how much wider the characterization ranges are than the normal operating ranges
_widen = [(p.prange[1] - p.prange[0]) / (p.nor[1] - p.nor[0]) for p in params]
widen_lo, widen_hi = min(_widen), max(_widen)

# Purpose and scope

The production bioreactor is the step at which A-Mab acquires most of the quality
attributes the drug substance must meet. Fed-batch culture forms the glycan distribution,
the charge variant distribution and the aggregate content of the harvested material, and
the platform purification train that follows (Protein A capture, low-pH inactivation,
cation exchange, anion exchange, virus filtration and formulation) modifies neither the
glycan nor the charge variant distribution. Experience with the platform establishes how a
humanized IgG1 culture behaves, but it does not fix the ranges over which A-Mab may be
operated at the receiving site. RA-001 ranked this step as the largest single source of
risk to product quality in the drug substance process, and assigned it the widest
characterization scope in the campaign.

This plan defines the studies that close that gap, and it defines them before they are
executed. It states which parameters will be varied and over what ranges, how the cultures
will be run and sampled, which validated methods will measure each attribute, and by what
criteria the operating region, the proven acceptable ranges and the parameter
classifications will be decided. The studies will be executed on a qualified scale-down
model of the commercial production bioreactor (§5.1), and the results, the classifications
and the resulting contribution to the control strategy will be reported in PCR-003.

The plan covers the `{python} n_par` process parameters listed in §6.1 and the
`{python} n_cqa_set` quality attributes the register assigns to this step. Four topics fall
outside it. Seed expansion up to and including the N-1 bioreactor is not characterized,
because RA-001 assessed it as a low risk to product quality, and the transfer of those
steps is covered by the parent transfer plan (PTP-001). Harvest and clarification are
covered by PCP-004, and no viral clearance is claimed for this step, so no spiking study is
planned here. Confirmation at commercial scale belongs to Stage 2 and to the
`{python} n_ppq` process performance qualification batches, so nothing in this plan should
be read as a claim about performance at `{python} f"{scale_l:,.0f}"` L.

# Objectives

The studies described in this plan have five objectives.

1. Quantify the effect of each characterized process parameter on each quality attribute
   the production bioreactor forms, over the characterization ranges given in §6.1.
2. Define a multivariate operating region in the well-controlled culture parameters within
   which every attribute in scope is predicted to meet acceptance.
3. Establish a proven acceptable range for every parameter and attribute pair the
   response-surface model covers, and determine whether the normal operating range falls
   inside each one.
4. Classify every parameter in scope under SOP-4001, including any parameter for which no
   effect is found.
5. Deliver the ranges, in-process controls and monitoring requirements that the control
   strategy and the Stage 2 qualification will rely on.

The first three objectives are quantitative and depend on the studies succeeding, while the
last two are decisions, and §7 fixes in advance the rules by which those decisions will be
made.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The production bioreactor is a fed-batch culture of a recombinant CHO cell line in a
stirred tank vessel, inoculated from the N-1 seed bioreactor and harvested after
`{python} f"{dur_sp:g}"` days at the set-point condition. Culture pH is held by carbon
dioxide sparging and base addition, temperature by the vessel jacket, and dissolved oxygen
by sparged air and oxygen, and bolus nutrient feeds are added on a fixed schedule. At
commercial scale the vessel is operated at `{python} f"{scale_l:,.0f}"` L working volume
(SOP-2003). At bench scale it is operated on the qualified model described in §5.1.

Four mechanisms shape what the studies expect to find, and the ranges in §6.1 follow from
them. Galactosylation depends on the activity of the Golgi galactosyltransferase and on the
supply of the nucleotide sugar donor (UDP-galactose), both of which fall as a culture ages
and as the extracellular environment acidifies. High mannose is set earlier in the same
pathway, by how far mannosidase trimming has progressed before the antibody is secreted,
which makes it sensitive to lumenal pH and to temperature. Afucosylation reflects a
competition instead. Core fucosyltransferase acts on the antibody while it transits the
Golgi, so a condition that slows transit raises the fucosylated fraction and lowers
afucosylation. Deamidation and aggregation are not enzymatic at all, and both accumulate
with the time the secreted antibody spends in an ageing broth, which is why culture
duration is carried as a factor of both multivariate designs (§6) and is expected to act on
several attributes at once.

Prior product knowledge supports this framing without replacing it. The platform has
produced three earlier humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) in the same
medium and feed system, and several of the A-Mab acceptance criteria in @tbl-cqa were set
from X-Mab clinical experience [@amab2009]. Since the mechanisms above are properties of
the host cell line and of the culture chemistry, they may be carried across products. The
effect sizes may not. They depend on the specific productivity and the glycan profile of
the individual clone, so the studies characterize A-Mab directly, and prior knowledge is
used only to justify the factor set and the ranges.

## Quality attributes in scope

@tbl-cqa lists the quality attributes the register assigns to this step, each with an
acceptance criterion, a level of criticality and a Tool #1 score. Criticality is treated as
a continuum and not as a binary classification [@ichq9; @amab2009]. The Tool #1 score is
the product of the impact of an attribute on safety or efficacy and the uncertainty in that
impact, and attributes at high or very high criticality (H or VH) are treated as critical.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print()
print(": Quality attributes formed at the production bioreactor, with acceptance criteria, "
      "criticality and Tool #1 score. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

High mannose is the only attribute of very high criticality and carries the highest Tool #1
score in @tbl-cqa, so it is treated as the governing attribute of the step and the
operating region will be judged against it first. Afucosylation and galactosylation come
next, both linked to antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC), which is the
primary mechanism of action of A-Mab, and both formed only in the bioreactor. Aggregate is
also of high criticality. However, this step shares control of aggregate with cation
exchange (PCR-007), so a harvest level inside acceptance is necessary and is not
sufficient.

Acidic charge variants sit at the other end of the range, at very low criticality. The
attribute is measured on every run nonetheless, since deamidation is a stability-indicating
change and a large shift would be informative even where the acceptance criterion is as
wide as this one.

Host cell protein and residual DNA are formed here and cleared downstream, and this step
sets the load that the capture column will see, so both will be measured on the harvest of
every run to characterize that load. Neither is a response of the designed experiments. The
clearance credit for both belongs to Protein A capture (PCR-005), cation exchange
(PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008), and PCMR-001 consolidates it across the train.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 assessed every process parameter of this step by risk ranking and filtering. Each
parameter received one score for the potential to affect a critical quality attribute and a
second for the potential to interact with other parameters, and the two scores together
decided the study type [@amab2009]. Parameters scoring high on both went into the
multivariate design, since an interaction can only be estimated when the interacting
parameters are varied together. Parameters with a credible main effect and little
interaction potential were assigned to univariate assessment. No parameter of this step was
left unstudied.

`{python} n_mv` of the `{python} n_par` parameters are therefore studied multivariately and
`{python} n_uv` univariately (@tbl-par). The split is not a statement about which
parameters matter, which is what the studies exist to determine. It is a statement about
which parameters are expected to act through the same chemistry and so have to be varied
together.

The characterization ranges are wider than the normal operating ranges throughout, by
factors between `{python} f"{widen_lo:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{widen_hi:.1f}"`. Two
considerations set that width: a range has to be wide enough for a real effect to be
resolved above assay and process noise, and wide enough to bound a knowledge space that can
support later movement within the design space without new studies. It also has to stay
inside what the equipment can deliver and inside conditions the culture survives. Dissolved
carbon dioxide is varied over a range that is wide in proportion to the set-point
(@tbl-par), because it accumulates at commercial scale in a way a bench vessel does not
reproduce without deliberate control.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The studies will be executed in bench-scale stirred tank bioreactors qualified as a model
of the commercial vessel (SOP-1001). Qualification is a precondition of execution and not
an outcome of it, so no characterization run may start before the qualification report is
approved.

The model rests on a standard division between scale-independent and scale-dependent
variables: the first are set to the values the commercial process will use, and the second
are set so that performance matches across scales [@amab2009]. Culture pH, temperature,
dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration, feed schedule and culture duration are
scale-independent, and the bench vessels will run them at commercial target values.
Agitation, gas flow rates, headspace pressure and working volume are scale-dependent, and
each will be set to match the commercial vessel on volumetric mass transfer coefficient,
impeller tip speed and the pCO₂ profile through the culture.

Qualification compares the model with at-scale data on inputs and on outputs. The input
attributes are the seed train material and the medium and feed lots. The output attributes
are the viable cell density profile, viability at harvest, titre and the
`{python} n_resp` quality attributes the designed experiments will measure. The model is
qualified when no statistically significant difference is found between the bench and the
commercial distributions of these attributes at the set-point condition. The qualification
package is filed under SOP-1001 and will be referenced, not repeated, in PCR-003.

Two limits of the model should be stated in the sections that rely on it. A bench vessel
mixes in seconds where a `{python} f"{scale_l:,.0f}"` L vessel takes minutes, so any
gradient effect at commercial scale is under-represented at bench scale. Carbon dioxide
also strips more readily from a small vessel, which is why pCO₂ is controlled as an
independent factor in these studies (§6.1) instead of being allowed to find a level of its
own. Neither limitation is removed by this plan. Both are managed by carrying pCO₂ as a
characterized factor and by confirming the attributes at commercial scale during Stage 2.

The centre point runs of both designs serve a second purpose: replicated at the set-point
of every factor, they estimate pure error, which is the reference against which lack of fit
is tested (§5.5).

## Cell line, media and culture operation

The cell line is the A-Mab production clone, expanded from a single vial of the working
cell bank through the seed train to the N-1 bioreactor. Seed expansion is run at platform
conditions and is not characterized here (§1). Each characterization run will be inoculated
from an N-1 culture meeting the platform criteria for viable cell density and viability, so
that the input to the study is controlled and is not itself a source of variation.

Basal medium and feeds are prepared under SOP-2004 from the platform formulation. Medium
and feed lots are identity tested and released against specification before use, and they
are inputs controlled to specification and not variables under characterization, with one
exception. Basal medium concentration is a univariate factor of this study (§6.4), and the
levels will be prepared as separate lots to the same formulation.

The production culture is operated under SOP-2003, with bolus feeds added on the platform
schedule and harvest at the duration the design assigns to the run. Culture duration is a
factor of the multivariate designs and may not be allowed to float, so a run that reaches
the platform stop criterion for viability before the assigned duration departs from the
design and will be handled as a deviation (§9).

## Analytical methods

Every attribute in scope is measured by a validated method, and @tbl-sop gives the
procedure and the validation reference for each. Released N-glycan mapping by 2-AB
HILIC-UPLC (SOP-3010, AMV-3010) reports afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose
from a single analysis, so the three glycan attributes come from one sample and share a
common analytical variance. Size variants are measured by SEC-HPLC (SOP-3011, AMV-3011),
which reports the high molecular weight fraction, and charge variants by icIEF (SOP-3013,
AMV-3013), which reports the acidic fraction. Host cell protein is measured by ELISA
(SOP-3012, AMV-3012) and residual host cell DNA by qPCR (SOP-3014, AMV-3014).

Method performance is not restated in this plan. Accuracy, precision, specificity, range
and quantitation limits are given in the validation report cited for each method in
@tbl-sop, and PCR-003 will quote the relevant precision estimate wherever an effect is
small enough for assay variance to matter.

Samples for a given attribute will be analysed in as few analytical sequences as the sample
count allows, and a common reference standard will be included in every sequence. Since a
design is analysed as a whole, an analytical batch effect that tracked the run order would
be indistinguishable from a factor effect.

## Sampling plan

Sampling has two purposes: process monitoring follows the culture while it runs, and the
harvest sample characterizes what the culture produced.

Monitoring samples will be drawn daily from each vessel and tested for viable cell density,
viability and the platform metabolite panel (SOP-2003). Offline pH, dissolved oxygen and
pCO₂ will be measured on the same sample and compared with the online probe readings, and
that comparison is the control that detects probe drift during a run.

The harvest sample is the study sample. One clarified harvest sample per run will be taken
at the end of culture and tested for every attribute named in §5.3, and retained aliquots
will be stored frozen so that a repeat test or an additional test can be run without
repeating the culture.

Replication is concentrated at the centre point, where the screening design carries
`{python} n_scr_cen` runs and the response-surface design carries `{python} n_rsm_cen`, all
at the set-point of every factor. These runs estimate the reproducibility of the whole
system, from culture through assay, and they supply the pure error term used in §5.5. The
factorial and axial runs are not replicated, which is the usual trade in a designed
experiment: precision on the effects is bought from the structure of the matrix instead of
from repetition.

## Statistical methods

All models will be fitted on coded factors, each coded so that the set-point maps to zero
and the edges of the characterization range map to ±1, which puts every factor on a common
scale and makes the coefficients comparable (SOP-1002).

The screening design will be analysed by ordinary least squares (OLS) with all main effects
and all two-factor interactions in the model, and terms will be tested at α = 0.05. An
effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, so it is the change in the response
across the whole characterization range of the factor.

The screening model identifies the factors that matter, and it is not a predictive model:
it estimates `{python} n_scr_terms` terms from `{python} n_scr` runs, which leaves
`{python} scr_res_df` residual degrees of freedom, `{python} scr_pe_df` of them pure error
and `{python} scr_lof_df` lack of fit. A model that near-saturated fits the data it was
built on closely whatever the truth is. Its coefficients will therefore be used to select
factors and directions, and not to predict a response at a setting the design did not run.

The response-surface design will be analysed as a full quadratic model in the
`{python} n_rsm_f` factors carried forward, with all main effects, all two-factor
interactions and all quadratic terms. It estimates `{python} n_rsm_terms` terms from
`{python} n_rsm` runs, which leaves `{python} rsm_res_df` residual degrees of freedom,
`{python} rsm_pe_df` of them pure error and `{python} rsm_lof_df` lack of fit. This is the
predictive model, and the operating region, the proven acceptable ranges and the capability
estimate are all derived from it.

Model adequacy will be reported as R², adjusted R², predicted R² from the PRESS statistic,
the model F statistic and an ANOVA lack-of-fit test against pure error. Residual
diagnostics will be reported for every response: residuals against predicted values, a
normal quantile plot, and predicted against actual values.

Capability at commercial scale will be estimated by simulation. `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"`
batches will be simulated by drawing each parameter from within the normal operating range,
predicting each attribute from the fitted response-surface model, adding the residual
variance of that model, and computing a one-sided capability index against the acceptance
criterion. The simulation uses a fixed random seed, so the reported values are reproducible.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

@tbl-par lists every parameter in scope with the set-point, the range to be studied, the
normal operating range and the study type. @tbl-code gives the letter codes used for the
multivariate factors in the design matrices and in the analysis.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
print()
print(": Process parameters of the production bioreactor, with the ranges to be studied "
      "and the study type assigned by RA-001. {#tbl-par}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Coded factor legend for the multivariate designs. {#tbl-code}")
```

The two ranges in @tbl-par do different jobs. The normal operating range is the band within
which the commercial process will be controlled, and it is the band the capability
simulation draws from (§5.5). The range studied is wider, and it is the edge of the
knowledge space: it is where the studies look for the setting at which an attribute leaves
acceptance. A proven acceptable range is determined inside the range studied and is
reported per attribute (§8), so the range studied is not itself a proven acceptable range.

Culture pH, culture temperature, dissolved carbon dioxide, osmolality and culture duration
are the multivariate factors. All five act on the same intracellular chemistry, either
through the pH and temperature dependence of the Golgi glycosyltransferases or through the
time the antibody spends in culture, so interactions between them are expected and have to
be estimable. By contrast, dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration, basal
medium concentration and nutrient feed volume act mainly on cell growth and nutrient
supply. RA-001 scored the potential for these four to interact with the glycosylation
chemistry as low, and they are assessed one parameter at a time (§6.4).

## Screening design

The screening study is a two-level fractional factorial design in the `{python} n_scr_f`
multivariate factors augmented with centre points, comprising `{python} n_scr_fac`
factorial runs and `{python} n_scr_cen` centre point runs, or `{python} n_scr` runs in all.
The fraction is a half replicate of Resolution V, so every main effect and every two-factor
interaction is estimable clear of the others, and only interactions of three factors and
above are aliased with the terms of interest (Appendix A).

Runs will be executed in randomized order across the available vessels, with the centre
point runs distributed through the campaign instead of grouped. Randomization is the
control against a time trend in the vessels, in the medium lots or in the assay.

The purpose of the screening study is to identify which factors and which interactions have
an effect large enough to matter, and in which direction. It is not intended to produce a
model that predicts (§5.5).

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design (CCD) in
`{python} n_rsm_f` of the screening factors, comprising `{python} n_rsm_fac` factorial
runs, `{python} n_rsm_ax` axial runs and `{python} n_rsm_cen` centre point runs, or
`{python} n_rsm` runs in all. The axial points sit on the faces of the coded cube instead
of outside it, so no run is executed beyond the characterization ranges in @tbl-par, and
that choice gives up some rotatability to buy a design that stays inside conditions the
vessels can hold and the culture can survive (Appendix B).

The factors carried forward are culture pH, culture temperature, culture duration and
dissolved carbon dioxide. Although the matrix in Appendix B is written on the assumption
that screening confirms these four, screening may identify a different set. The matrix will
then be re-issued before execution, which is an amendment to this plan and not a deviation
from it.

This design adds the curvature terms the screening design cannot estimate. It is the source
of the operating region in §7, of the proven acceptable ranges in §8 and of the capability
estimate in §5.5.

## Univariate assessment

Dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration, basal medium concentration and
nutrient feed volume will be assessed one parameter at a time. Each will be run at the low
edge and at the high edge of the characterization range in @tbl-par, with every other
parameter held at the set-point, which gives `{python} n_uv_cond` culture conditions in
all. The centre point runs of the screening design provide the set-point comparator, since
they already sit at the set-point of every parameter in the study.

A study that varies one parameter at a time cannot detect an interaction between the
parameter varied and the parameters held fixed. That limitation is accepted on the risk
basis in §4.3, where these four parameters were scored as unlikely to interact with the
chemistry that forms the glycan attributes. However, if a univariate result contradicts
that expectation, the parameter will be added to a follow-up multivariate design, and the
addition will be reported in PCR-003.

A parameter with no detectable effect is still a result. Any such parameter will be
classified under SOP-4001 on the evidence of the range it was held over, and that range
will be retained in the knowledge space as evidence that the attributes are robust to the
parameter.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The studies will be judged against the rules in this section, and the rules are stated
before execution so that the judgement does not depend on what the data turn out to be.

The scale-down model is qualified when the bench and the commercial distributions of the
input and output attributes listed in §5.1 show no statistically significant difference at
α = 0.05 at the set-point condition. Where a difference is found, the model will be
modified and requalified before any characterization run is executed. A model that cannot
be qualified for one attribute may still be used for the others, provided PCR-003 states
which claims it does not support.

A fitted model is adequate when the lack-of-fit test against pure error is not significant
at α = 0.05, and when the adjusted and predicted R² are reported beside R² so that
over-fitting is visible. Predicted R² is the most informative of the three here, since it
is computed by leaving each run out of the fit in turn. A model that fails the lack-of-fit
test will not be used to define an operating region, and the response concerned will
instead be augmented with further runs or reported as characterized univariately, with
PCR-003 stating which was done and why.

A term is retained in a model when it is significant at α = 0.05, and a term that is not
significant may still be retained where it is the lower order term of a significant
interaction or quadratic, because dropping it changes the interpretation of the term above
it. Terms retained on that basis will be identified as such.

The operating region will be declared over the part of the characterized space in which the
response-surface model predicts that every attribute the step governs meets acceptance. It
will be reported as a multivariate region and not as a set of independent parameter ranges,
since the region is bounded by interactions between the factors. Movement within the region
is not a change to the process, and movement outside it requires change control [@ichq8;
@ichq10].

Capability will be reported as a one-sided index for every attribute in scope, with the
margin between the simulated mean and the acceptance limit stated alongside it. No numeric
minimum for the index is fixed by this plan. That criterion is defined per study, because a
meaningful minimum depends on the criticality of the attribute and on how detectable an
excursion would be, and neither of those is a property of the simulation.

Each parameter will then be classified under SOP-4001 into one of four classes. A parameter
is a critical process parameter (CPP) when variation within the ranges studied affects a
critical quality attribute and there is a real risk of operating outside the design space.
It is a well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) when the same impact exists but
the parameter is easy to hold, so the risk of an excursion is low. It is a key process
parameter (KPP) when it affects process performance without affecting product quality. It
is a general process parameter (GPP) when no impact on a critical quality attribute is
demonstrated over the range studied. Classification rests on the demonstrated effect and on
the control capability together, and PCR-003 will give the reason for each parameter.

The study as a whole passes when the scale-down model is qualified, when an adequate model
exists for every attribute the step governs, when an operating region containing the whole
normal operating range can be declared, and when every parameter carries a classification
with a stated reason. Failure against any of these is not a failure of the plan. It will be
reported in PCR-003 as a finding, together with the action taken.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

The operating region defined in §7 is multivariate, and a multivariate region is an awkward
thing to write into a batch record. Each parameter will therefore also be reported with a
proven acceptable range (PAR) for every attribute the response-surface model shows it to
govern. A proven acceptable range is the univariate form of the same information.

The acceptance basis comes first: each attribute will be judged against the drug substance
acceptance criterion in @tbl-cqa. Where the control strategy establishes an in-process
limit on the harvest for an attribute, the proven acceptable range will be determined
against that limit instead, because an intermediate has to meet a criterion that applies to
the intermediate. PCR-003 will state which criterion was used for each attribute.

Two analyses will be run for every pair of a parameter and an attribute. The first holds
the other factors at their set-points and scans the parameter of interest across the full
characterization range, evaluating the fitted response-surface model on a grid of
`{python} par_grid` points. The second propagates the normal operating ranges of the other
factors: at each grid point, `{python} f"{par_mc:,}"` values of every remaining factor are
drawn from within the normal operating range, the fitted model is evaluated at each draw,
the residual variance of the model is added, and the 95 % predictive interval of the
attribute is computed.

The decision rule differs between the two analyses, and it does so deliberately. In the
first, the proven acceptable range is the contiguous span of the parameter, containing the
set-point, over which the predicted mean stays within acceptance. In the second it is the
contiguous span over which the whole 95 % predictive interval stays within acceptance. The
second is a robustness criterion and will normally give the narrower range. Where the two
coincide across the entire characterization range, the parameter is acceptable everywhere
it was studied and is robust to the rest of the operating point moving within the normal
operating range as well.

Every governed attribute will be reported with a two-panel plot against the governing
parameter, which is the response-surface factor carrying the largest main effect on that
attribute. The panels show the two analyses side by side, with the acceptance limit drawn,
the acceptable region shaded green, and the set-point and the normal operating range
marked.

The relationship to the operating region should be read carefully. A proven acceptable
range is univariate, so it holds for the one parameter it names under the conditions of the
analysis that produced it. It is not a licence to move two parameters to opposite edges at
once. Where a proven acceptable range covers the whole characterization range, the binding
constraint on the process is the corner of the multivariate region and not that range. Both
results are bounded by the characterization ranges in @tbl-par, by the fitted
response-surface model and by the conditions the scale-down model represents (§5.1).

# Data management and integrity

Data generated under this plan are held to the same integrity requirements as manufacturing
records. Raw data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, and
they are complete, consistent, enduring and available.

Culture data are captured by the bioreactor control system and retained as the raw record.
Analytical data are captured in the laboratory information management system (LIMS), and
the calculations that turn instrument output into a reportable result are performed by
validated templates. Study design, run assignment and statistical analysis are recorded in
the electronic laboratory notebook (ELN), and the analysis scripts are held under version
control, so a reported number can be traced back to the data and to the code that produced
it.

Every record is reviewed by a second qualified person before it is used, and a correction
leaves the original entry legible and carries the reason and the date. Audit trails are
enabled on all systems and are reviewed as part of that data review.

This plan is a controlled document, so a change to the design, to the ranges or to the
acceptance criteria after approval requires an approved amendment before the affected runs
are executed. A departure discovered after execution is recorded as a deviation,
investigated for root cause, and assessed for impact on the study conclusions in PCR-003.

# Roles and responsibilities

@tbl-roles assigns the work across the functions that execute and approve this plan.
Process Development owns the plan, the execution and the report, and Manufacturing Science
and Technology (MSAT) owns the scale-down model and the link to the receiving site.
Analytical Development owns the methods and the analytical data, Statistics owns the
designs and the model fitting, and Quality Assurance approves both this plan and PCR-003.

| Function | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Process Development | Authors this plan, executes the cultures, interprets the results, writes PCR-003 |
| Manufacturing Science and Technology | Qualifies and maintains the scale-down model; confirms that set-points and ranges are implementable at the receiving site |
| Analytical Development | Performs the assays in §5.3, maintains method validation, reports analytical performance |
| Statistics | Approves the designs, performs the model fitting, the capability simulation and the proven-acceptable-range analysis |
| Quality Assurance | Approves this plan and PCR-003, dispositions deviations, confirms data integrity |
| Manufacturing, receiving site | Reviews the resulting ranges and control requirements for commercial implementability |

: Functions and responsibilities for the execution of this plan. {#tbl-roles}

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-003, which will report the executed studies, the
operating region, the proven acceptable ranges, the capability estimate and the parameter
classifications. The scale-down model qualification report is a prerequisite deliverable
and is filed separately under SOP-1001.

The work runs in a fixed order, with model qualification first because it gates everything
after it. The screening study follows, with `{python} n_scr` runs, and analysis of the
screening data then confirms or revises the factors carried into the response-surface
design, with any revision issued as an amendment before execution (§6.3). The
response-surface study follows, with `{python} n_rsm` runs. Once the screening result is
available the univariate conditions of §6.4 may be executed in parallel with it, since they
do not depend on the response-surface runs. Analysis, capability simulation, classification
and reporting come last.

`{python} n_runs_total` cultures are planned in all. No calendar dates are fixed here: the
sequence is fixed, and the campaign schedule is maintained under PCMP-001.

# Risks and assumptions

Three assumptions carry the study, and each has a risk attached to it.

The first is that the scale-down model represents the commercial vessel closely enough for
a conclusion drawn at bench scale to hold at `{python} f"{scale_l:,.0f}"` L. Qualification
tests that at the set-point condition only, and it does not test it at the edges of the
characterization ranges, so the assumption is weakest exactly where the operating region is
most constrained. The risk is managed by carrying pCO₂ as a characterized factor, since it
is the parameter that differs most between the two scales, and by confirming the attributes
at commercial scale during Stage 2.

The second is that screening identifies the right subset of factors to carry into the
response-surface design. A factor with a real effect that screening failed to resolve would
be excluded from the predictive model and would not appear in the operating region at all.
The risk is managed in two ways: every factor not carried forward is held at the set-point
through the response-surface runs, so an excluded factor contributes no variation to the
fitted model, and each is classified on the screening evidence with the range that evidence
supports.

The third is that platform and prior product knowledge transfer to A-Mab. The mechanisms
transfer, because they are properties of the host cell line and of the culture chemistry,
but the effect sizes may not, because they depend on the clone. As a result the studies
characterize A-Mab directly, and prior knowledge is used only for the factor set and the
ranges (§4.1).

Two operational risks remain. A change of medium or feed lot during a campaign of
`{python} n_runs_total` cultures could introduce a step change confounded with run order,
and the controls are randomization (§6.2) and the use of a single lot per component
wherever the campaign length allows. Assay variability may also be large in comparison with
a small effect near an acceptance limit, and the controls there are the replicated centre
points, which estimate the combined culture and assay variance directly, and the precision
estimates in the method validation reports.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when it is approved by the functions listed in @tbl-appr. Approval
signifies that the study design, the ranges, the analytical methods and the decision
criteria are agreed before execution, and that a change to any of them requires an
amendment under §9.
